implementation_notes: Play models the pattern as action composition: an ActionBuilder builds the reusable security stack, ActionRefiner/ActionFilter/ActionTransformer specialize it - authentication narrows Request to a user-carrying request, permission checks refine further - and andThen composes the pieces into the action that finally calls the controller block. The base action is therefore a composed action pipeline rather than a superclass, while cross-cutting concerns that must apply to every request go into HTTP filters. Keep the refinements small and ordered, because andThen establishes the sequence.
code_sketch:
val userAction = new UserAction(controllerComponents.parsers.default)
val SecureAction = userAction.andThen(PermissionCheckAction)

def update(id: String) = SecureAction { request =>   // request: UserRequest
  Ok(orders.update(id, request.username))
}
pitfalls: andThen order is the security order; swapping refinements changes what each one can see and can drop the permission check.
Body parsing happens before action composition by default, so a rejected request may still have been parsed; enable deferred body parsing when that matters.
Composing action functions changes the request type, so the business block can rely on the refined type only if it is written against the last refinement.
